note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world - how many courts a park has, when the gates open - come from the City of Las Vegas's and the City of Henderson's own pages and are cited. Claims about our own coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Clark County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. This is the first county in Nevada this directory has published in, and one city of it is Las Vegas, published first, the other Henderson, published second; both are on this page. Henderson's pages were read in a browser because cityofhenderson.com answers scripted requests with HTTP 403, and every count row and address block was saved as text and is re-asserted on every build.

slots.coverage: Two cities in Clark County are published here: Las Vegas, with five venues and nineteen courts verified against the City's own pages, and Henderson, with seven venues and 33 courts verified against three City of Henderson pages read in a browser. That is twelve venues and 52 courts with a source and a date on each. Nothing else in the county has been read. North Las Vegas has not been read; Clark County's own parks department has not been read; neither appears on any page here, and this page does not characterise what either has. What is published in Las Vegas is five City parks whose court counts, addresses and park hours the City states: Durango Hills with seven courts, Aloha Shores and Lorenzi with four each, Centennial Hills and Patriot with two each. What is published in Henderson is two recreation centres and five parks: Black Mountain Recreation Center with 18 outdoor courts, Silver Springs Recreation Center with four of which three are indoor, Mission Hills Park with three shared with tennis, and Aventura Park, Siena Heights Trailhead, Sonata Park and Sunridge Park with two shared with tennis each. Both cities count more than publishes, and the missing venues are named on each city page rather than dropped: three in Las Vegas holding sixteen courts, and seven in Henderson, six holding seventeen courts and the seventh a practice wall. In every case but the wall, the missing fact is an address.
slots.distribution: What is verified in this county sits in two cities, and the shape differs between them. Las Vegas spreads nineteen courts across five parks with no complex among them; its largest count, Durango Hills' seven, is at a park built around an 18-hole executive golf course, and the largest count the City states, Police Memorial's eight, is absent for want of an address that resolves. Henderson gathers more than half of its 33 at one address, Black Mountain Recreation Center's 18, under a City heading that says "OUTDOOR PICKLEBALL COURTS", and holds the county's only published indoor courts, three at Silver Springs Recreation Center under "INDOOR PICKLEBALL COURTS". The two cities also keep their records differently. Las Vegas counts on two records, a parenthesis in a park page's amenity list and a line in the City's pickleball post of 11 March 2026; three of its venues are counted on both and two, Lorenzi and Patriot, on the post alone. Henderson counts on one record, its pickleball page, whose five headings carry the only indoor and outdoor words in the county, and prints its addresses in a separate park directory and on facility pages. Eleven of Henderson's courts are under "PICKLEBALL & TENNIS COMBINED", shared with tennis and on no stated side. Neither city states a surface, a price or a light for any court. Las Vegas states park hours of 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. at every venue; Henderson states no hours at all.
slots.gaps: The honest position is that this is a two-city page wearing the heading of a county, and the gap will not close by accident. North Las Vegas has not been read. Clark County's own parks have not been read. The threshold has not moved - three venues with a named source and a date - and neither operator has been given the chance to clear it yet. What this county does supply is the difference between a court existing and a court being publishable, twice over. The City of Las Vegas counts thirty-five courts at eight parks on one post, and nineteen are here; the City of Henderson counts fifty at thirteen facilities on one page, and 33 are here. The missing thirty-three fail on boring facts. In Las Vegas, two addresses no resolver finds and one the City never prints. In Henderson, six addresses - Blooming Cactus, Dundee Jones, Montagna, Whitney Mesa, Weston Hills and the Downtown Recreation Center - that neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap finds as the City writes them, and a seventh facility, Whitney Ranch, refused because the City lists it under "INDOOR PICKLEWALL COURTS" and a wall is not a court. None of the refusals is about the courts being real; both cities state each count plainly. The second gap is inside the published twelve: lighting, price and surface are not stated for any court in the county, so a reader gets a count, an address and, in Las Vegas, a clock. Clubs, commercial venues and homeowners' associations may hold courts in this county; none publishes a source this site has read, so none is listed, and that absence is about who writes things down rather than about where the game is played.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Clark County?
faqs.a: We do not know, and no honest page can tell you. What we have checked is 52 courts across twelve venues - 19 at five Las Vegas parks and 33 at seven Henderson venues - each with a source and a date you can see. The two cities together count 85 on their own pages; 33 of those are at addresses neither resolver finds or the City does not print, or are a practice wall.

faqs.q: Why are only Las Vegas and Henderson listed?
faqs.a: Because they are the two operators in the county whose courts have been checked against a named source. A city appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source_url and a date_checked. North Las Vegas and Clark County's own parks have not been read. Henderson's site refuses scripted fetches with a 403, so its pages were read in a browser.

None that either operator states. The City of Las Vegas says nothing about lighting on any park page or its pickleball post, and the City of Henderson says nothing on its pickleball page, park directory or facility pages, so all 52 courts are recorded as unknown. Las Vegas's park hours of 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. are a fact about the gate, not the lamps.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Not stated, in either city. Las Vegas publishes no price; "Drop in for a pop-up game" on its post is a play format rather than a fee. Henderson publishes no price either and says only that courts can be reserved by calling its Sports Office. A venue is called free here only when the operator writes it down, so no Las Vegas or Henderson venue is called free.

faqs.q: Which venue in the county has the most courts?
faqs.a: Black Mountain Recreation Center in Henderson, with 18, printed as one row under the City's "OUTDOOR PICKLEBALL COURTS" heading; the park directory lists the same address as "Black Mountain Pickleball Park" with parking and restrooms. In Las Vegas the largest published count is Durango Hills Park's seven; Police Memorial Park's eight is unpublished for want of an address that resolves.

faqs.q: Are there indoor courts in Clark County?
faqs.a: Three that an operator states: Silver Springs Recreation Center in Henderson, under the City's "INDOOR PICKLEBALL COURTS" heading, with a fourth court under a heading that gives no side. Henderson also counts three indoor courts at its Downtown Recreation Center, but "50 Van Wagenen St." resolves nowhere. Las Vegas states neither indoor nor outdoor for any court.

faqs.q: How often is this checked again?
faqs.a: These pages were read on 7 September 2026, and every quoted sentence is snapshotted into the repository that builds this site and re-asserted on every build. If either City changes a count, prints an address for a refused facility, or moves Whitney Ranch under a pickleball heading, the build fails and someone reads the page again - in a browser, for Henderson.
